cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 takes up the Forecaster's T2 evidence plan and attacks its witnesses; T5 answers directly.
cells.limitation: T3 pivots to method without answering T2's challenge that the doubt itself may be fog.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T5 splits the milestone from the good it promises; T6, T8 and T9 build on that split.
cells.limitation: T11 adds no new distinction; it restates the Experimenter's opening value.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T1 versus T2: whether the user's doubt is honest signal or forecasting fog.
cells.limitation: After T2 nobody returns to trusting present doubt; Section D lists it as unresolved.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T9 adopts T8's loneliness reframe; T10 narrows the Detective's claim in response.
cells.limitation: T11 asserts residual disagreement ('agree on less') that the turns never actually show.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D: feeling behind and wanting the milestone are separate signals.
cells.limitation: T11 ends on a general principle rather than sharpening the open question about trusting doubt.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T4 states the Forecaster's plan accurately before naming its sunk-cost bias.
cells.limitation: T8 answers 'withdrawing from friends', which T7 never proposed; T7 suggested noticing private envy.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T4 names the assumption that lived reports are neutral; T5 answers by widening the sample.
cells.limitation: T8's rebuttal of T7 rests on a misreading, so the auditions objection goes partly unanswered.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T3 quotes Mill's 'experiments of living', consistent with On Liberty; Girard and Gilbert fairly paraphrased.
cells.limitation: T6, T8, T11 mark Mill's 1859 book pd=false, contradicting T3; T10 calls housing markets deadlines.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T8 offers loneliness as 'Maybe behind is really lonely', clearly a hypothesis.
cells.limitation: T1 states the user's desire as fact: 'Your friends have not shown you something you want.'

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T10: 'I concede that', then narrows to the feeling telling almost nothing.
cells.limitation: The Detective never answers T2's point that the doubt itself may be unreliable.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A: discomfort may concern belonging, security or time with friends, not the milestones.
cells.limitation: Comparison-driven self-worth beyond loneliness is named in A but barely pursued in T1-T11.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T8 uses friends' attention moving to new households to reframe 'behind' as loneliness.
cells.limitation: T6 builds its trials on renting and being single, details the user never gave.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T11 keeps skipping milestones legitimate, matching the user's stated doubt.
cells.limitation: T11 closes on the Experimenter's own value of 'tried and chosen', not the user's priority.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T9 and T10 raise real time windows such as biology.
cells.limitation: T6 invents context: assumes the user rents and is single ('Rent another year', 'date').

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on what stings, when the pull fades, and real time limits, each with implications.
cells.limitation: Relationship and housing status are assumed in T6 instead of asked or branched.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T5 offers security and being chosen, T8 loneliness, as alternatives; Section D asks which draws you.
cells.limitation: T1 asserts the user does not want the milestones before hedging.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T1: 'Behind implies a finish line, and nobody here agreed to one.'
cells.limitation: The assumption that friends set the yardstick is examined; family or age norms are not.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T8 sets self-authored choice against the cost to friendship.
cells.limitation: No turn asks the user which matters more, connection or independence, when they conflict.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T1 contagion, T6 dread, T11 embarrassment: social pressure named without pathologising.
cells.limitation: Family expectations and age-related fear never appear in T1-T11.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T8 'Envy is data, not a verdict'; Section D poses a question the user can answer.
cells.limitation: T10 says the feeling tells 'almost nothing', discounting the user's own signal.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Options include waiting (T9), small trials (T6) and addressing connection (Section E).
cells.limitation: Options stay scattered across turns; no turn or section states the choice set plainly.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T8 prices withdrawal; T9 says indefinite waiting is not neutral.
cells.limitation: T6 calls trials cheap; the money and time costs of milestones or trials go unweighed.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: pull strongest when comparing, fading alone, favours the Detective's reading.
cells.limitation: T6's 'another year' and 'a month of weekends' are not derived from the user's facts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section E names real time limits as the decisive fact to learn early.
cells.limitation: Other unknowns in Section E are not ranked by consequence against one another.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: Section E: look up actual constraints, talk with people on different paths, including none.
cells.limitation: 'Addressing connection directly' in Section E gives no concrete first step.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T1 'wanting spreads like a yawn' makes mimetic desire plain.
cells.limitation: Section E's 'the goal and the road have come apart' is slightly abstract.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T4 names 'The Forecaster wants reports' instead of an ambiguous pronoun.
cells.limitation: T8 'the second half and reject the first' maps loosely onto T7's halves.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Eleven turns, all within 25 to 65 words.
cells.limitation: Section E packs four branches into one dense paragraph.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Detective suspicious (T4, T7), Forecaster empirical (T5), Experimenter methodical (T6).
cells.limitation: The Forecaster's register in T5 and T9 is plainer and closer to the Experimenter's.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns rarely recap; each adds a move.
cells.limitation: T11 and Section D partly restate earlier points without adding new ones.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T8 loneliness and T9 closing windows give the feeling real stakes.
cells.limitation: T1-T7 keep the stakes abstract before T8 grounds them.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T10 concedes, traced to T9's windows argument, and narrows its claim.
cells.limitation: T10's concession is modest and expected rather than surprising.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T7: 'auditions for the same script... with you as the understudy.'
cells.limitation: The Forecaster (T2, T5, T9) has less personality than the other two.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T6 'Cheap tests beat a verdict reached by dread'; T1 yawn analogy.
cells.limitation: The Forecaster's turns contain no line as memorable as the others'.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T8 shifts from method to loneliness, a real emotional turn.
cells.limitation: T11 closes on a flat general principle, losing T8-T10's momentum.

strengths: T5's split of milestone from the good it promises is used by T6, T8 and T9.
Section E branches on conditions the user can observe, each tied to an option.
T4-T5 objection and answer on biased witnesses; T10's concession names its cause.
weaknesses: T6 assumes the user rents and is single, and calls trials cheap without pricing them.
T8 rebuts withdrawal from friends, a position T7 never took.
T11 ends on the Experimenter's own value rather than the user's open question.

symptoms.observed: Proposes trials built on renting and dating, details the user never gave.
symptoms.evidence: Rent another year, ... date without a plan attached.

symptoms.observed: Calls the trials cheap without naming their costs or the milestones' costs.
symptoms.evidence: Cheap tests beat a verdict reached by dread.

symptoms.observed: Answers withdrawal from friends, which T7 did not propose.
symptoms.evidence: Withdrawing from friends is also an experiment, and it has a cost.

symptoms.observed: States the user's lack of desire as fact before hedging.
symptoms.evidence: Your friends have not shown you something you want.

symptoms.observed: Closes on a general principle instead of the sharpened open question.
symptoms.evidence: Then we agree on less than we pretended, and that is fine.

findings.description: Mill's On Liberty (1859) is marked pd=false in T6, T8, T11 but pd=true in T3.
Runner counted 2 quotation marks in pd=false turns; the only candidates are plural possessives (friends'), not quotations.
Treats a housing market as a real deadline comparable to biology, without support.
Quotation 'experiments of living' matches recollection of On Liberty ch. 3; no source attached to confirm.

rubric_fit_notes: The pd_false quotation-mark FAIL appears to count possessive apostrophes in T6 and T8; no established quotation in a pd=false turn, so no cap. The user's message is a self-reflection rather than an explicit choice, so C5 cells were read as the basis for a tentative direction.
question_type_note: Read as a decision question labelled self_reflection, so C5 credited branches toward small steps rather than a single life choice.
